resources.string: By downloading the code-switching model you agree to the Hebrish terms of use: free for personal and non-commercial use; commercial use, including telephony, needs a licence.

The Hebrish models are free for personal, research, education and non-profit use. Commercial use, including telephony and call centres, needs a commercial licence: access-requests@hebrish.app. Hebrish is experimental and trained on one speaker\'s voice; transcripts can be wrong, so check them before relying on them. It is provided as is, without warranty. Your audio stays on this phone.
On-device voice typing with NVIDIA Parakeet TDT 0.6B v2. Made for the English-Hebrew code-switching model; stock Parakeet is there too. Recognition runs on the phone; audio never leaves it.
Delete %1$s from this phone? You can download it again later.
Download failed: %1$s. Tap Download to resume.
Checking Hugging Face for a newer model…
Update available: %1$s (%2$d MB). %3$s stays in use until the new model is downloaded and verified, then it is deleted.
%1$s\nStandard sherpa-onnx int8 files: other apps with file access can load them from here.
Can\'t use that folder. Pick a folder on internal storage or an SD card.
Needed to hear you. Audio never leaves the phone.
Not enabled yet. Turn on “Hebrish” in the system keyboard list.
Use HeliBoard as your main keyboard. Its mic key opens Hebrish, and once the text is in you are taken back to HeliBoard. In HeliBoard: Settings → Toolbar (or Preferences) → show the voice input key.
Return to previous keyboard after inserting
Tap here, switch to Hebrish, and speak…

Using the code-switching model? Its website has the results and every model, dataset and demo. Report a bug, ask for a feature or send feedback by email to feedback@hebrish.app, suggest a Hebrew word it gets wrong, or send voice samples to help it learn more voices.
No email app found. Write to %1$s.
Paused at %1$d:%2$02d. Resume, or tap ■ to insert.
Take discarded. Tap the mic to speak.
No text field to type into. Tap a field, then Insert last.
Tap a text field first, then Insert last.

Automatic: the keyboard you came from
Long-press the keyboard key in Hebrish to open the system keyboard picker at any time.
Model not downloaded. Tap the mic to open setup.
Microphone not granted. Tap the mic to open setup.
Too short. Tap the mic to try again.
Heard nothing. Tap the mic to try again.

Shows a floating microphone over other apps. Tap it to dictate into the text field you are in, without switching keyboards. Hebrish reads the focused text field only to put your transcript in at the cursor, and it never reads password fields. Audio and text stay on this phone.

A mic button that floats over every app. Tap it in any text field, talk, and tap Stop: the text goes in at the cursor and your keyboard stays as it is. While you talk it shows Pause, Retake and Discard. If no text field had focus when the text was ready, the mic shows Insert: tap a field, then Insert. Long-press the idle mic to insert the last transcript again. It runs as an accessibility service.
The floating mic is on. Drag it to move it, also while you talk (by the mic or the bar), or set its place below.
The floating mic is off. Turn on “Hebrish floating mic” in Accessibility settings, under Downloaded apps (or Installed apps). The guide below goes through it step by step.
Show only while a text field is focused
Insert the transcript into the focused text field
No text field to type into. Tap one, then tap Insert on the mic. The text is on the clipboard too.
Tap a text field first, then Insert.
Turn it on: step by step
Left or right edge: the mic snaps to that edge when you drag it. Anywhere: it stays exactly where you drop it.
Bar background while you talk: %1$d%% opaque
While you talk the mic is always red.
Long takes, and whether text goes in while you talk, are set on the Dictation screen.
It also needs the microphone: see the guide.
This field doesn\'t accept dictation; the text is on the clipboard.
Long takes, and typing as you talk
%1$s is not downloaded yet. Tap to download.
On. Opens from your keyboard\'s mic key.
Off. Optional: a mic over every app.
Download any model, whether or not it is the one in use; each is about 660 MB, once. Downloads run one after another. The model in use is the one the keyboard and the floating mic transcribe with.
Waiting: downloads after the current one.
New versions of downloaded models are looked for when the app opens, at most every 6 hours. A model being updated stays usable until the new version is downloaded and checked.
A voice keyboard that opens from your regular keyboard\'s mic key, records, types the text in and switches back.
Done: the floating mic is on.
The floating mic is off. Go through the steps below; each button opens the right settings page, and this screen updates when you come back.
Open Accessibility settings, then Downloaded apps (on some phones Installed apps or Installed services), then Hebrish floating mic. Turn it on and tap Allow. If that works, skip to the last step.

Android 13 and later block accessibility for apps installed from an APK. Trying step 1 once shows a “Restricted setting” message; after that, open App info, tap ⋮ (top right), then Allow restricted settings, and confirm with your PIN or fingerprint. The ⋮ item only appears after that first try.
Back in Accessibility settings → Downloaded apps → Hebrish floating mic, the switch now works. Turn it on and tap Allow.
The floating mic records with the app\'s microphone permission.

Some phones (OnePlus, Xiaomi, Samsung and others) stop background apps to save battery, and the floating mic disappears until you turn it on again. Allow Hebrish to run unrestricted. On OnePlus, also check App info → Battery → Unrestricted.
Battery: optimised. Android may stop the floating mic.
A mic now sits at the edge of the screen. Tap into a text field, tap the mic, talk, and tap it again. Drag it to move it.

Takes can run up to %1$d minutes. While you talk, each stretch of speech is transcribed at the next pause, so when you tap stop only the last few seconds are left to do. The keyboard, the floating mic and Try it all work this way.

Off: the whole take goes in when you tap stop, and Discard throws all of it away. On: each part goes in as soon as it is transcribed, so long dictations appear while you talk; Discard then only drops the part not yet typed.

The model is loaded once and kept in memory. The floating mic loads it as soon as a text field gets focus, so it is ready by the time you tap. Silence at the start and end of a take is skipped. The very first take after the phone restarts still waits a few seconds for the model to load.
If the text has nowhere to go

Floating mic: if no text field has focus when the text is ready, the mic shows Insert. Tap a field, then Insert, and the text goes in at the cursor. It is on the clipboard too. Voice keyboard: Insert last transcript does the same.

Installed from an APK? An APK doesn\'t update itself. Hebrish has its own F-Droid repository: add it once, and every new version arrives as an ordinary app update. It is the same app, signed with the same key, so F-Droid updates this install and keeps your models and settings. It also works in Droid-ify and Neo Store.
1. Install F-Droid, if you don\'t have it
F-Droid asks to add the repository: confirm. Then search F-Droid for Hebrish. New releases reach the repository within six hours.
No F-Droid app found. Opening the repository in the browser.

This link always gives the newest APK. Install it over this one to update; you keep your models and settings.

Hear what it does before you set it up as a keyboard.
Tap the mic, say a sentence, then tap again to stop. The text appears below. Nothing leaves your phone.
